claim: Added hook time can be repaid only where the original wastes some: a delay the game pads with, a fixed-length uncontended copy, the game's own long routine at 28 MHz, or a plot after the game's sync.

evidence.text: The game pads each pass to ten figures' time with its own delay, so every hook's time can be repaid there to the T-state: +0.1 % in JNext against +2.1 % in the approved build.
evidence.quote: the game pads each pass to ten figures' time with its own delay, so every hook's time can be repaid there to the T-state;

evidence.text: The update delay scales with the droid count (DD80) and with 6 or more blocks there is none, so hook time is not absorbed by a frame lock and must be repaid.
evidence.quote: the update delay scales with the droid count (DD80), so hook time is not absorbed by a frame lock; it must be repaid.

evidence.text: Pace was won by running the game's own 21 ms scroll at 28 MHz (21 ms down to 4), not by polishing the colour work.
evidence.quote: Pace was won by running the game's own 21 ms scroll at 28 MHz, not by polishing the colour work.

evidence.text: When every plot follows the game's own sync and takes a fixed time, a part of it at 28 MHz pays for hooks that vary, with no wait.
evidence.quote: When every plot follows the game's own sync and takes a fixed time, a part of it at 28 MHz pays for hooks that vary, with no wait;

evidence.text: A game that waits for FRAMES needs no limiter round its plots: the wait takes up the time.
evidence.quote: A game that waits for FRAMES needs no limiter round its plots: the wait takes up the time.
